summary: O-018 is now exercised against a real stalled SMB session, with no admin rights, no Defender change and no impacket. Both prechecks passed first. Defender let SMBLibrary 1.5.8.1 and SMBLibrary.Win32 1.5.8 load. The Windows 11 client, with its default settings including required signing, authenticated to an SMBLibrary server on 127.0.0.1 on a spare port through a non-persistent `New-SmbMapping -TcpPort` and listed the share. The new opt-in test, StalledShareTests.CancellingAScanOfAShareThatStoppedAnsweringNeverHangsInTheClose, serves a real folder normally until one folder's listing, then answers nothing more. It passed. The measurement is that Cancel() returns in about 1 ms, but the SMB client holds the unanswered listing, and the canceller's CancelSynchronousIo with it, until it gives up on the server: the scan returned 61.9 s and 66.0 s after Cancel in two runs. It then ends Cancelled, with the stalled folder not committed and its handle closed on a pool thread. The rest of the build from fdf77d6 is untouched; the default suite still passes 117/117 with the new test left out.

files.why: Holds the O-018 test (opt-in, Trait Network=SMB-LOOPBACK); the LoopbackShare fixture, an SMBLibrary server on 127.0.0.1 on a spare port with a test user, reached through a non-persistent New-SmbMapping -TcpPort and removed afterwards; and StallingFileStore, which wraps NTDirectoryFileSystem, answers normally until the listing of one folder, then answers nothing until released.

Adds SMBLibrary 1.5.8.1 and SMBLibrary.Win32 1.5.8 (LGPL-3.0-or-later) to the test project only, and extends the default VSTestTestCaseFilter to leave SMB-LOOPBACK tests out of runs that name no filter.
Replaces 'stalled session: spike 3 never ran' with the measurement (62 to 66 s after Cancel, Cancel() still prompt, ends Cancelled, close off-thread) and documents the opt-in loopback SMB test.
Records both prechecks with commands and outputs, the fixture faults met, and the measurement table.
Output of the connection precheck, with the user's own unrelated mapping filtered out.
The run with a 2 s bound: still blocked 2 s after Cancel, with the canceller's one CancelSynchronousIo itself blocked.
The measurement run with a 150 s bound: the scan returned 65,987 ms after Cancel.
The final test, run by its case command: passed, returning 61,865 ms after Cancel.

obligations.how: StalledShareTests.CancellingAScanOfAShareThatStoppedAnsweringNeverHangsInTheClose feeds the shape directly. An established, signed SMB2/3 session to a loopback SMBLibrary server stops answering at the listing of 'hung', and every request after it (close, cancel, anything else) goes unanswered too. The test passed by its case command. It asserts that Cancel() returns in under 250 ms (measured 0.9 ms) and that the scan returns within the SMB client's own limit, 90 s (measured 61.9 s; 66.0 s in the measurement run). It asserts the result is Cancelled, never Completed, with no unreadable entries, 'hung' not committed and never reported as listed, and no orphan entries. It asserts the aborted listing's handle was handed to the pool closer (ClosesHandedOff 1); the close was not pending when the scan returned. Measured and not hidden: criterion (1)'s 2 s does not hold for this shape, because the SMB client keeps the CancelSynchronousIo itself blocked until it gives up on the server. The design already lists stalled sessions as outside that guarantee.

tests.command: [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes on every SMBLibrary and SMBLibrary.Win32 package DLL
tests.note: Precheck 1: all six DLLs read in full, so Defender flagged none. Both libraries also loaded and ran.

Precheck 2: New-SmbMapping -TcpPort 63243 and then 63269 exited 0 with Status OK. The server logged a successful session setup for the test user (client OS 10.0.26100) and the tree connect. The share listed in 16 ms, and Remove-SmbMapping exited 0.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx -nologo --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.StalledShareTests..."   (runs 1-4 while building the fixture)
tests.note: Fixture faults, all fixed. (1) A null handle in DeviceIOControl crashed the test host. (2) SMBLibrary threw NotImplementedException on class 60 and crashed the host. (3) The crashed host left a non-persistent mapping, so the next New-SmbMapping failed with error 53 and then with 'more than one port'. I removed my own stale mapping and made the fixture clear its own pattern.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx -nologo --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.StalledShareTests.CancelReturnsFromAScanStalledOnAShareThatStoppedAnswering"   (2 s bound)
tests.note: A real result: 2 s after Cancel the scan was still blocked. The canceller showed 1 attempt and 0 delivered, meaning its CancelSynchronousIo was itself blocked in the SMB client. Cancel() took 0.7 ms.

tests.command: same filter, with the bound temporarily 150 s (measurement)
tests.note: The scan returned 65,987 ms after Cancel. CancelSynchronousIo made 1 attempt and was delivered after about 66 s. The result was Cancelled with no unreadable folders and 'hung' uncommitted. The close was handed off and was not pending when the scan returned.
The final test, run by its case command: 1 passed in 1 m 3 s. The scan returned 61,865 ms after Cancel, and Cancel() took 0.9 ms.
Default suite: 117 passed, 0 failed. The SMB-LOOPBACK and TEST-NET-1 tests are left out by the default filter. Afterwards, Get-SmbMapping showed 0 mappings to 127.0.0.1.

deviations: The rebuild note asked that 'the scan returns within a set time after cancel'. On this shape the time is the SMB client's own limit, not Cancel's: the client keeps the unanswered QUERY_DIRECTORY, and the CancelSynchronousIo aimed at it, until it gives up on the server, measured at 61.9 and 66.0 s. The test therefore asserts a 90 s bound and says why. It does not assert criterion (1)'s 2 s, which the design (m6) already excludes for stalled sessions. Nothing in-process can make the 2 s hold here; only abandoning the scan thread, the design's rejected fallback, would.

The note says the hung folder must be 'reported as an error, not Completed with 0 files'. The test asserts Status Cancelled, never Completed, with the hung folder not committed and never reported as listed. It does not add an Unreadable entry, because criterion (2) makes a 995 under a requested cancel a cancellation, not an unreadable folder. The listing's result is discarded whatever the client finally returned.

Two additions the note did not name. SMBLibrary.Win32 is added next to SMBLibrary, for NTDirectoryFileSystem, a real-folder INTFileStore; SMBLibrary itself ships none. And SMBServer's public Start listens only on port 445, which Windows' own server holds, so the fixture calls SMBServer's private Start overload that takes a port, through reflection. Both are in the test project only.

The fixture store answers STATUS_INVALID_INFO_CLASS where SMBLibrary would throw on a class it cannot encode: FileIdExtdDirectoryInformation (60), which the Windows client passes through. That is how a server without the class behaves, and the scanner then lists with FILE_FULL_DIR_INFO. So this test runs the fallback listing class, not the extended one.
follow_ups: Design decision for a person: if a share that stops answering mid-session drops, Cancel leaves the scan blocked for 62 to 66 s, and the UI stays in 'cancelling' for that long. The only in-process remedy is the design's rejected fallback: stop awaiting the scan thread on Cancel and let it finish in the background. If that wait is not acceptable, it belongs back at design-slice.

O-003 (owed to validate-slice) now has evidence on the stalled shape. The aborted listing's close ran on a pool thread and was not pending when the scan returned. The scan thread is never held by the close; what holds it is the listing itself, until the SMB client gives up.

The stalled-share test takes about 65 s and needs the Windows 11 24H2 SMB client (New-SmbMapping -TcpPort). It is opt-in for that reason and would fail on Windows 10, which the platform constraint still supports.
Scratch folders %TEMP%\taad-sl024-smb (the precheck) and %TEMP%\taad-sl024-respike (attempt 2) are left in place. Their sources and logs are copied into the slice, so both can be deleted.
